about.text: I’m a developer and a teacher. For more than 5 years I’ve been building web and mobile apps — from company websites to CRMs and internal tools. For the last 4 years I’ve worked at Stanford private school, where I’m now Head of IT: I set the standards for our lessons and build the school’s digital tools myself. I love turning messy processes run on spreadsheets and paper into clear systems that save people time.

projects.subtitle: A weekly assessment platform for a private school: ~400 students, 5 roles and a Telegram bot for parents.
projects.text: I moved the system from Google Sheets and Apps Script to Laravel + React with no data loss and scores that match to the point. Students take tests on school computers, teachers manage the question bank, and parents get their child’s weekly card right in Telegram.
projects.stack.label: Project stack

projects.student.p1: The timer runs on the server — reloading the page doesn’t reset it
projects.teacher.p1: Questions with images and reading passages
projects.teacher.p2: Bulk upload of questions from a file
projects.lead.p2: Breakdowns by school, class and group
projects.parent.p2: Percentages only — no grades and no red
projects.telegram.p1: A weekly picture card for every student
projects.telegram.p2: The card is rendered in the browser (SVG → JPEG) and sent without re-uploading
projects.arch.title: How it works
projects.arch.alt: Diagram: students, teachers, admins and parents use React + Inertia talking to a Laravel API; the API stores data in MySQL/PostgreSQL and Redis and connects to the Telegram bot, Excel import/export and a Google Sheets report.
projects.decisions.title: Interesting decisions
projects.decision1.title: Exact scoring
projects.decision1.text: Final scores combine the test and written work with per-subject weights; rounding matches the old system to the point.
projects.decision2.title: Reliable submission
projects.decision2.text: Server-side time and writes in a locked transaction: a double click never creates a second attempt.
projects.decision3.title: Duplicate-free import
projects.decision3.text: Uploading the same Excel file again duplicates nothing — rows are matched by hash.
projects.decision4.title: Security
projects.decision4.text: Codes are stored as HMAC hashes, brute force is throttled and permissions are checked on every action.
crm.title: CRM for a property developer
crm.subtitle: Apartment sales from first enquiry to final payment: unit grid, deals, reservations, contracts, installments and reports. Namangan, Uzbekistan.
crm.text: Built an MVP from scratch in 7 days for a residential developer: managers run clients and deals and reserve apartments right in the unit grid, while the system fills in the contract from the client’s own template, calculates the installment schedule and reminds buyers about payments in Telegram. The interface is in Uzbek and Russian.
crm.tabs.label: System sections
crm.chess.p1: Reserve right from the unit grid
crm.deals.p2: Reservations with a timer and extension
crm.installments.p1: Rounded to 1,000 sum; the schedule always adds up to the total
crm.installments.p2: Payments are allocated across the schedule automatically
crm.contract.p1: Contract built from the client’s Word template
crm.contract.p2: Amount in words and transliteration to Cyrillic
crm.contract.p3: Data is frozen: later edits to the client don’t change a signed contract
crm.telegram.p1: Reminder to the buyer 3 days before a payment
crm.telegram.p2: One-click bot connection for the buyer
crm.arch.alt: Diagram: managers and admins work through React 19 + Inertia with Laravel (Actions, Policies); Laravel stores data in PostgreSQL with locks, CHECK constraints and unique indexes, and drives a queue for PDFs via LibreOffice, a scheduler that expires reservations and a Telegram bot for reminders.
crm.decision1.title: No double sales
crm.decision1.text: A reservation runs in one transaction that locks the apartment, backed by a unique index in the database. A test with two concurrent Postgres sessions proves it: the second reservation is rejected.
crm.decision2.title: Reservations always expire
crm.decision2.text: The scheduler releases expired reservations every 5 minutes, and every screen double-checks them before rendering — even if cron goes down.
crm.decision3.title: Installments to the last sum
crm.decision3.text: The schedule and payment allocation are pure functions: the preview and the saved result always match, whatever order the operations run in.
crm.decision4.title: Statuses as a state machine
crm.decision4.text: “Reserved” only through a reservation, “sold” only through a contract. Every change is written to the history.
